`tdh.h` is actually win32 api header and etwdump only builds for WIN32. The `validate-clang-check.sh` performs check on Linux. @crondaemon @alagoutte should `validate-clang-check.sh` be skipped and/or ignored here?
@desowin , other than this build failure, do you have any other comments for this PR?

> should `validate-clang-check.sh` be skipped and/or ignored here?

No, tools/validate-clang-check.sh should be modified to add etwdump.c and etw_message.c to its list of files to ignore, so change it to do

    # extcap/{etwdump.c,etl.c,etw_message.c}: those compile, and are compiled,
    # only on Windows
    if test \( "$FILE_BASENAME" = "etwdump.c" -o \
               "$FILE_BASENAME" = "etl.c" -o \
               "$FILE_BASENAME" = "etw_message.c" \)
    then
        continue
    fi

(Changing the script to *selectively* remove files from the list, depending on the build configuration, is left as an exercise to the reader.)
@guyharris , I updated validate-clang-check.sh as you instructed, but it still fail as before. Could you please help to check if I did something wrong in validate-clang-check.sh?

My suggested changes depend on *previous* changes I've made to validate-clang-check.sh.  Please rebase your change on top of the current state of the main branch (you will probably have to resolve some conflicts with my changes; that will involve replacing

```
# extcap/etl.c: that compiles, and is compiled, only on Windows
if test "$FILE_BASENAME" = "etl.c"
then
    continue
fi
````

in the main branch with

```
# extcap/{etwdump.c,etl.c,etw_message.c}: those compile, and are compiled,
# only on Windows
if test \( "$FILE_BASENAME" = "etwdump.c" -o \
           "$FILE_BASENAME" = "etl.c" -o \
           "$FILE_BASENAME" = "etw_message.c" \)
then
    continue
fi
```
pipeline passed, if you are good with the update, could you please merged this PR? Thanks
